Grammar Point: A あるいは B (A aruiwa B)
Meaning: Indicates alternatives; 'A or B', 'either A or B'.
Formation: Phrase A + あるいは + Phrase B
Example (Japanese): 今日は映画を見るあるいはショッピングをする予定です。
Example (Romaji): Kyou wa eiga wo miru aruiwa shoppingu wo suru yotei desu.
Example (English): Today, I plan to either watch a movie or go shopping.

Meaning: Expresses that in addition to A, there is also B; 'moreover', 'besides', 'not only', 'but also'.
Formation: Sentence A + おまけに  + Sentence B
Example (Japanese): 彼は遅刻した。おまけに宿題も忘れた。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa chikoku shita. Omake ni shukudai mo wasureta.
Example (English): He was late. Moreover, he forgot his homework.

Meaning: Indicates a sudden change or shift in the topic or situation; 'now then', 'well', 'so'.
Formation: A + さて + B
Example (Japanese): 今日の仕事が終わった。さて、これから帰るか。
Example (Romaji): Kyou no shigoto ga owatta. Sate, kore kara kaeru ka.
Example (English): Today's work is done. Now then, shall we go home?

Meaning: Expressing additional information; 'moreover', 'besides', 'furthermore'.
Formation: Statement A + 。しかも + Statement B。
Example (Japanese): この料理は美味しいです。しかも、安いです。
Example (Romaji): Kono ryouri wa oishii desu. Shikamo, yasui desu.
Example (English): This dish is delicious. Moreover, it is cheap.

Grammar Point: A。したがって B。(A. Shitagatte B.)
Meaning: Express a cause-and-effect relationship; 'therefore', 'consequently', 'so'.
Formation: A + したがって + B
Example (Japanese): 今日は雨が降っています。したがって、傘を持って行きましょう。
Example (Romaji): Kyou wa ame ga futteimasu. Shitagatte, kasa wo motte ikimashou.
Example (English): It is raining today. Therefore, let's bring an umbrella.

Grammar Point: A すなわち B。 (A sunawachi B)
Meaning: Express that A is equivalent to B; 'in other words', 'namely', 'that is to say'.
Formation: Phrase A + すなわち + Phrase B
Example (Japanese): 私は立派な成果を出したい、すなわち、成功したいのです。
Example (Romaji): Watashi wa rippana seika wo dashitai, sunawachi, seikou shitai no desu.
Example (English): I want to achieve great results, in other words, I want to succeed.

Meaning: Indicates that when action A is done, action or event B follows; 'then', 'when', 'if'.
Formation: A (Sentence) + すると + B (Sentence)
Example (Japanese): 電話をかけると、彼女が出ました。
Example (Romaji): Denwa wo kakeru to, kanojo ga demashita.
Example (English): When I made the phone call, she answered.

Meaning: Recalling something related to A; 'speaking of which', 'by the way', 'now that you mention it'.
Formation: A + そういえば + B
Example (Japanese): 映画。そういえば、彼は映画館で働いているんだ。
Example (Romaji): Eiga. Souieba, kare wa eigakan de hataraite irun da.
Example (English): Movies. Speaking of which, he works at a movie theater.

Meaning: Expresses 'therefore' or 'because of that'.
Formation: A + そこで + B
Example (Japanese): 明日は試験があります。そこで今晩勉強しようと思います。
Example (Romaji): Ashita wa shiken ga arimasu. Soko de konban benkyou shiyou to omoimasu.
Example (English): There is an exam tomorrow. Therefore, I plan to study tonight.

Meaning: Expressing 'that's what A is; in other words, B'.
Formation: A (Statement)。それが B (Restatement or explanation of A)。
Example (Japanese): 彼は勉強ができる。それが天才だ。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa benkyou ga dekiru. Sore ga tensai da.
Example (English): He can study well. That's what a genius is.

Meaning: Express a sequence of events; 'and then', 'so', 'because of that'.
Formation: Sentence A +。それで+ Sentence B。
Example (Japanese): 昨日は雨が降っていた。それで公園に行かなかった。
Example (Romaji): Kinou wa ame ga futte ita. Sore de kouen ni ikanakatta.
Example (English): It was raining yesterday. So, I didn't go to the park.

Meaning: Expresses 'even so', 'nevertheless', 'still', or 'but'; used to contrast two statements.
Formation: A (situation) + 。それでも + B (action or thought)
Example (Japanese): 今日は日曜日です。それでも、仕事に行かなければなりません。
Example (Romaji): Kyou wa nichiyoubi desu. Sore demo, shigoto ni ikanakereba narimasen.
Example (English): Today is Sunday. Nevertheless, I have to go to work.

Meaning: Express contrast or a contradiction between two situations or facts; 'even though', 'despite', 'but still'.
Formation: A。それなのに B。
Example (Japanese): 彼は頭がいい。それなのに、試験に落ちた。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa atama ga ii. Sore nanoni, shiken ni ochita.
Example (English): He is smart. Despite that, he failed the exam.

Grammar Point: A。それなら B。(A. Sore nara B.)
Meaning: Express 'if that's the case, then'; used to show a logical consequence or decision based on a given situation.
Formation: Situation A (sentence) + 。それなら + Situation B (sentence)
Example (Japanese): 試験が近い。それなら、もっと勉強しなければならない。
Example (Romaji): Shiken ga chikai. Sore nara, motto benkyou shinakereba naranai.
Example (English): The exam is coming soon. If that's the case, I must study more.

Grammar Point: A それはそうと B。 (A Sore wa sou to B)
Meaning: Changing the topic; 'by the way', 'speaking of which'.
Formation: Sentence A + それはそうと + Sentence B
Example (Japanese): それはそうと、今日の天気はいいですね。
Example (Romaji): Sore wa sou to, kyou no tenki wa ii desu ne.
Example (English): By the way, the weather is nice today, isn't it?

Meaning: Expresses contrasting ideas or statements; 'but', 'however'.
Formation: Sentence A + だが + Sentence B
Example (Japanese): このレストランは値段が高い。だが、味はとてもいい。
Example (Romaji): Kono resutoran wa nedan ga takai. Daga, aji wa totemo ii.
Example (English): This restaurant is expensive. But, the taste is very good.

Meaning: Express contrast between two situations; 'although', 'but', 'however'.
Formation: Sentence A + ただ + Sentence B
Example (Japanese): 彼は頭がいい。ただ、努力はあまりしない。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa atama ga ii. Tada, doryoku wa amari shinai.
Example (English): He is smart; however, he doesn't make much effort.

Meaning: Adding a condition or exception to a statement; 'however', 'provided that', 'but only if'.
Formation: Statement A + ただし + Condition B
Example (Japanese): この部屋を使ってもいいです。ただし、使った後で掃除してください。
Example (Romaji): Kono heya wo tsukatte mo ii desu. Tadashi, tsukatta ato de souji shite kudasai.
Example (English): You can use this room. However, please clean up after you use it.

Meaning: Used to give a reason, express cause or bring up a topic; 'because', 'since', 'it's just that'.
Formation: Verb-casual + だって、い-Adjective + だって、な-Adjective + だって、Noun + だって
Example (Japanese): 暇だって、映画を見に行こうよ。
Example (Romaji): Hima datte, eiga wo mi ni ikou yo.
Example (English): Since we are free, let's go watch a movie.

Grammar Point: A。ちなみに B。(A. Chinamini B.)
Meaning: Used to give additional information about the topic; 'by the way', 'incidentally'.
Formation: A。ちなみに B。
Example (Japanese): 今日は授業がありません。ちなみに、明日も休みです。
Example (Romaji): Kyou wa jugyou ga arimasen. Chinamini, asu mo yasumi desu.
Example (English): There's no class today. By the way, tomorrow is also a day off.

Grammar Point: A。ということは B。 (A. To iu koto wa B.)
Meaning: Expresses the meaning 'if A, that means B' or 'A implies B'.
Formation: A + ということは + B
Example (Japanese): 彼女が泣いている。ということは何か悲しいことがあったに違いない。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo ga naite iru. To iu koto wa nanika kanashii koto ga atta ni chigainai.
Example (English): She is crying. That means something sad must have happened.

Grammar Point: A。というのは B。(Toiu no wa~)
Meaning: Used to give an explanation or provide additional information for A; 'that is to say', 'in other words'.
Formation: [Statement A]。というのは、[Statement B]。
Example (Japanese): 彼は非常に疲れています。というのは、昨夜、車で遠くまで行ってきたためです。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa hijou ni tsukareteimasu. to iu no wa, sakuya, kuruma de tooku made itte kita tame desu.
Example (English): He is very tired. That is to say, because he went far by car last night.

Meaning: Provides additional information; 'moreover', 'besides', 'in addition'.
Formation: A (sentence) + なお + B (sentence)
Example (Japanese): 明日は休みです。なお、月曜日も休みです。
Example (Romaji): Ashita wa yasumi desu. Nao, getsuyoubi mo yasumi desu.
Example (English): Tomorrow is a holiday. Moreover, Monday is also a holiday.

Meaning: Express contrasting opinions or facts; 'although', 'but', 'however'.
Formation: Clause A + もっとも + Clause B
Example (Japanese): 彼は頭がいい。もっとも、勉強も大切だ。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa atama ga ii. Mottomo, benkyou mo taisetsu da.
Example (English): He is smart. However, studying is also important.

Grammar Point: A。要するに B。(A. Yousuru ni B.)
Meaning: Expressing 'in short', 'in a nutshell', or 'to sum up' when restating or summarizing A as B.
Formation: A。要するに B。
Example (Japanese): このプロジェクトは成功しました。要するに、私たちのチームは素晴らしい仕事をしました。
Example (Romaji): Kono purojekuto wa seikou shimashita. Yousuru ni, watashitachi no chiimu wa subarashii shigoto o shimashita.
Example (English): This project was successful. In short, our team did a great job.

Meaning: Indicates the reason, cause, or condition for something; 'due to', 'regarding', 'per'.
Formation: Noun + につき
Example (Japanese): 試験につき、今日は静かにしてください。
Example (Romaji): Shiken ni tsuki, kyou wa shizuka ni shite kudasai.
Example (English): Due to the exam, please be quiet today.

Meaning: Expresses location or means; 'at', 'in', 'by', 'with'.
Formation: Noun + にて
Example (Japanese): 駅前広場にてイベントが開催されます。
Example (Romaji): Ekimae hiroba nite ibento ga kaisai saremasu.
Example (English): An event will be held at the station square.

Grammar Point: Noun の ことだから (Noun no koto dakara)
Meaning: Used to provide a reason or explanation based on one's knowledge about the noun; 'since', 'because', 'knowing'.
Formation: Noun + のことだから
Example (Japanese): 彼は料理が得意なのことだから、美味しい料理を作ってくれるでしょう。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa ryouri ga tokui na no koto dakara, oishii ryouri wo tsukutte kureru deshou.
Example (English): Since he is good at cooking, he will probably make us delicious food.

Grammar Point: Noun を はじめ (Noun wo hajime)
Meaning: Meaning 'starting with', 'including', 'not only... but also'.
Formation: Noun + をはじめ
Example (Japanese): 日本料理をはじめ、さまざまな料理がこのレストランで楽しめます。
Example (Romaji): Nihon ryouri wo hajime, samazama na ryouri ga kono resutoran de tanoshimemasu.
Example (English): You can enjoy various dishes in this restaurant, starting with Japanese cuisine.

Grammar Point: Noun を はじめとして (Noun wo hajimete shite)
Meaning: Expresses 'starting with', 'beginning with', or 'including'.
Formation: Noun + をはじめとして
Example (Japanese): 東京をはじめとして、日本にはたくさんの観光スポットがあります。
Example (Romaji): Toukyou wo hajimete shite, Nihon ni wa takusan no kankou supotto ga arimasu.
Example (English): There are many tourist spots in Japan, starting with Tokyo.

Grammar Point: Noun を はじめとする Noun (Noun wo hajimete suru Noun)
Meaning: Indicates a representative example of a group; 'starting with', 'including', 'such as'.
Formation: Noun1 を はじめとする Noun2
Example (Japanese): 彼はフランス語をはじめとする外国語が話せる。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa furansugo wo hajimete suru gaikokugo ga hanaseru.
Example (English): He can speak foreign languages, starting with French.

Grammar Point: Noun を めぐって (Noun wo megutte)
Meaning: Concerning; with regard to; about
Formation: Noun + を + めぐって
Example (Japanese): 環境問題をめぐって、多くの議論が行われています。
Example (Romaji): Kankyou mondai wo megutte, ooku no giron ga okonawareteimasu.
Example (English): Many discussions are held concerning environmental issues.

Grammar Point: Noun を めぐる Noun (Noun wo meguru Noun)
Meaning: Indicate a situation or event revolving around a particular noun; 'concerning', 'regarding', 'pertaining to'.
Formation: Noun1 + を + めぐる + Noun2
Example (Japanese): この事件をめぐる議論が続いています。
Example (Romaji): Kono jiken wo meguru giron ga tsuduiteimasu.
Example (English): The debate concerning this incident continues.

Grammar Point: Noun を もとに (Noun o moto ni)
Meaning: Based on; drawing from; using as a reference.
Formation: Noun + をもとに
Example (Japanese): この映画は実話をもとに作られました。
Example (Romaji): Kono eiga wa jitsuwa o moto ni tsukuraremashita.
Example (English): This movie was made based on a true story.

Grammar Point: Noun を もとにして (Noun wo moto ni shite)
Meaning: Based on; using; utilizing.
Formation: Noun + をもとにして
Example (Japanese): 彼の意見をもとにして、計画を変更しました。
Example (Romaji): Kare no iken wo moto ni shite, keikaku wo henkou shimashita.
Example (English): Based on his opinion, we changed the plan.

Meaning: Means 'without doing', 'not doing', or 'without happening'.
Formation: Verb-stem + ことなく
Example (Japanese): 彼女は泣くことなく帰ってしまいました。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo wa naku kotonaku kaette shimaimashita.
Example (English): She went home without crying.

Grammar Point: Verb ないことには Verb ない (~nai koto ni wa ~ nai)
Meaning: Express that something cannot be done without meeting a certain condition.
Formation: Verb-ない + ことには + Verb-ない
Example (Japanese): 薬を飲まないことには、病気が治らない。
Example (Romaji): Kusuri o nomanai koto niwa, byouki ga naoranai.
Example (English): Unless you take the medicine, the illness won't get better.

Meaning: Expresses the outcome of a series of actions or events; 'in the end', 'finally', 'after'.
Formation: Verb-て + あげく, Noun + の + あげく, い/な-Adjective + あげく
Example (Japanese): 長い時間待ってあげく、電車が来なかった。
Example (Romaji): Nagai jikan matte ageku, densha ga konakatta.
Example (English): After waiting a long time, in the end, the train didn't come.

Meaning: Expresses the result of doing something excessively or beyond a certain point.
Formation: Verb-ます stem + あまり, い-Adjective + あまり,  な-Adjective + のあまり, Noun + のあまり
Example (Japanese): 昨日は疲れすぎたあまり、朝まで眠り続けました。
Example (Romaji): Kinou wa tsukaresugita amari, asa made nemuri tsuzukemashita.
Example (English): Yesterday, I was so tired that I slept until morning.

Meaning: Expresses doing something while a certain condition still holds; 'while', 'before', 'as long as'.
Formation: Verb-casual + うちに, い-Adjective + いうちに, な-Adjective + なうちに, Noun + のうちに
Example (Japanese): 元気なうちに、旅行を楽しんでください。
Example (Romaji): Genki na uchi ni, ryokou wo tanoshinde kudasai.
Example (English): Enjoy traveling while you are healthy.

Meaning: Expresses 'worth doing' for verbs.
Formation: Verb-stem + がい
Example (Japanese): この本を読むがいです。
Example (Romaji): Kono hon wo yomugai desu.
Example (English): This book is worth reading.

Meaning: Used to express that an effort is worth it or has value; 'to be worth the effort' or 'to pay off'.
Formation: Verb-casual (stem) + かいがあって
Example (Japanese): 毎日勉強するかいがあって、テストに合格した。
Example (Romaji): Mainichi benkyou suru kaiga atte, tesuto ni goukaku shita.
Example (English): It was worth the effort of studying every day, as I passed the test.

Meaning: Expresses the meaning of 'without worth', 'in vain', 'fruitless'.
Formation: Verb-ます stem + かいもなく, Verb-dictionary form + かいもなく
Example (Japanese): 長い間苦労したが、かいもなく失敗した。
Example (Romaji): Nagai aida kurou shita ga, kai mo naku shippai shita.
Example (English): I struggled for a long time, but in the end, it was all in vain and I failed.

Meaning: Indicates a process or action is 'in progress' or 'halfway'.
Formation: Verb-stem + かける
Example (Japanese): 彼女は食べかけのリンゴを置いて出かけた。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo wa tabekake no ringo wo oite dekaketa.
Example (English): She left a partially eaten apple and went out.

Meaning: Expresses that something tends to occur frequently or habitually.
Formation: Verb-ますstem + がち, い-Adjective stem + がち, な-Adjective stem + がち
Example (Japanese): 彼は風邪を引きがちです。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa kaze wo hikigachi desu.
Example (English): He tends to catch a cold easily.

Grammar Point: ～か～ないかのうちに (〜ka〜naika no uchi ni)
Meaning: Expresses an action that occurs immediately after another action; 'as soon as', 'no sooner than', 'the moment'.
Formation: Verb-casual + か + Verb-negative form + かのうちに
Example (Japanese): 駅に着くか着かないかのうちに、雨が降り出した。
Example (Romaji): Eki ni tsuku ka tsukanai ka no uchi ni, ame ga furidashita.
Example (English): The moment I arrived at the station, it started raining.

Meaning: Express the likelihood of a negative outcome or consequence.
Formation: Verb-stem + かねない
Example (Japanese): 彼はそんなに無責任だから、約束を守れかねない。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa sonna ni musekinin dakara, yakusoku wo mamore kane nai.
Example (English): He is so irresponsible that he might not keep his promise.

Meaning: Express inability or impossibility of doing an action.
Formation: Verb-ます stem + かねる
Example (Japanese): その問題は難しいので、私には解決できかねます。
Example (Romaji): Sono mondai wa muzukashii node, watashi niwa kaiketsu dekikanemasu.
Example (English): Since that problem is difficult, I cannot solve it.

Meaning: Express a similarity or comparison; 'as if', 'like', 'as though'.
Formation: Verb-casual + かのようだ, い-Adjective + かのようだ, な-Adjective + だかのようだ, Noun + だかのようだ
Example (Japanese): 彼は犬が怖いかのようだ。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa inu ga kowai ka no you da.
Example (English): He seems as if he is scared of dogs.

Meaning: Used to express a dilemma or indecision between two options or actions
Formation: Verb-ますform + か + Verb-ますform + まいか, い-Adjective + か + い-Adjective + であるまいか, な-Adjective + であるか + な-Adjective + であるまいか, Noun + であるか + Noun + であるまいか
Example (Japanese): このプロジェクトを引き受けるか引き受けないまいか、まだ決めていない。
Example (Romaji): Kono purojekuto wo hikiukeru ka hikiukenai maika, mada kimeteinai.
Example (English): I haven't decided whether to take on this project or not.

Meaning: Express the emphasis on the reason; 'precisely because', 'it is precisely because'.
Formation: Verb-casual + からこそ, い-Adjective + からこそ, な-Adjective + だからこそ, Noun + だからこそ
Example (Japanese): 失敗したからこそ、成功の意味がわかる。
Example (Romaji): Shippai shita kara koso, seikou no imi ga wakaru.
Example (English): It is precisely because I failed that I understand the meaning of success.

Meaning: Expresses that something is exceptional, unusual or negative from a certain aspect or point.
Formation: Noun + からして
Example (Japanese): 彼の顔つきからして、何か悪いことがあったのだろう。
Example (Romaji): Kare no kaotsuki kara shite, nanika warui koto ga atta no darou.
Example (English): From his facial expression, something bad must have happened.

Meaning: Expresses a judgment or evaluation based on a certain standard; 'from this perspective', 'considering', 'judging from'.
Formation: Noun + からすると
Example (Japanese): 経験からすると、この仕事は難しいでしょう。
Example (Romaji): Keiken kara suru to, kono shigoto wa muzukashii deshou.
Example (English): Considering their experience, this job might be difficult.

Meaning: Expresses 'just because...doesn't mean' or 'even though...not necessarily'.
Formation: Verb-casual + からといって, い-Adjective + からといって, な-Adjective + だからといって, Noun + だからといって
Example (Japanese): 雨が降ったからといって、試合が中止になるわけではありません。
Example (Romaji): Ame ga futta kara to itte, shiai ga chuushi ni naru wake de wa arimasen.
Example (English): Just because it rained doesn't mean the game will be canceled.

Meaning: Expresses a range of time, space or quantities; 'from...to', 'between...and', 'over'.
Formation: Noun 1 + から + Noun 2 + にかけて
Example (Japanese): 午前９時から午後５時にかけて、仕事をしています。
Example (Romaji): Gozen kyu-ji kara gogo go-ji ni kakete, shigoto wo shiteimasu.
Example (English): I work from 9 in the morning to 5 in the evening.

Meaning: Express a sense of responsibility or determination; 'since', 'now that', 'if'.
Formation: Noun + だ + からには, な-Adjective + だ + からには, い-Adjective + からには, Verb-casual + からには
Example (Japanese): 試験に合格したからには、一所懸命働かなければならない。
Example (Romaji): Shiken ni goukaku shita kara niwa, isshokenmei hatarakanakereba naranai.
Example (English): Since I passed the exam, I have to work hard.

Meaning: Express a perspective or point of view; 'from the standpoint of', 'in terms of', 'from the perspective of'.
Formation: Noun + から見ると
Example (Japanese): 費用から見ると、このプランはお得です。
Example (Romaji): Hiyou kara miru to, kono puran wa otoku desu.
Example (English): In terms of cost, this plan is a good deal.

Meaning: Express a judgment or opinion based on a specific criterion; 'speaking from', 'in terms of', 'from the viewpoint of'.
Formation: Noun + から言うと, Verb-casual + から言って, い-Adjective + から言って, な-Adjective + から言って
Example (Japanese): 値段から言うと、この商品が最もお得です。
Example (Romaji): Nedan kara iuto, kono shouhin ga mottomo otoku desu.
Example (English): Speaking from the viewpoint of price, this product is the best deal.

Meaning: Used to criticize someone for doing something contrary to their nature or appearance.
Formation: Verb-ますstem/い-Adjective + くせに, な-Adjective + なくせに, Noun + のくせに
Example (Japanese): 彼はいつも遅刻してくるくせに、自分が待たされるのが嫌いだ。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa itsumo chikoku shite kuru kuse ni, jibun ga matasareru no ga kirai da.
Example (English): He's always late, and yet he hates being kept waiting.

Meaning: Indicates the reason or basis for something; 'because', 'since', 'due to'.
Formation: Verb-casual + ことから, い-Adjective + ことから,な-Adjective + なことから, Noun + のことから
Example (Japanese): 彼は毎日運動することから、体が丈夫です。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa mainichi undou suru koto kara, karada ga joubu desu.
Example (English): Because he exercises every day, his body is strong.

Meaning: Used to express feelings or emotions towards a situation, an action, or an outcome.
Formation: Verb-casual + ことに, い-Adjective + ことに, な-Adjective + なことに, Noun + のことに
Example (Japanese): 彼が急に帰国することに驚いた。
Example (Romaji): Kare ga kyuu ni kikoku suru koto ni odoroita.
Example (English): I was surprised at him suddenly returning to his home country.

Grammar Point: ～ことになっている (〜koto ni natte iru)
Meaning: Expressing something is supposed to be or has been decided.
Formation: Verb-plain form + ことになっている, い-Adjective + ことになっている, な-Adjective + だ + ことになっている, Noun + だ + ことになっている
Example (Japanese): 日本では、左側を運転することになっています。
Example (Romaji): Nihon de wa, hidarigawa wo unten suru koto ni natte imasu.
Example (English): In Japan, it is decided that we drive on the left side.

Meaning: As long as, if only, providing that.
Formation: Verb-casual + さえ + ば, い-Adjective + さえ + いい, な-Adjective + さえ + いい, Noun + さえ + いい
Example (Japanese): お金さえあれば、幸せです。
Example (Romaji): O-kane sae areba, shiawase desu.
Example (English): As long as I have money, I am happy.

Meaning: To have no choice but to; cannot help but.
Formation: Verb-ない form (Drop ない) + ざるを得ない
Example (Japanese): この仕事は締め切りが近いので、残業するざるを得ない。
Example (Romaji): Kono shigoto wa shimekiri ga chikai no de, zangyou suru zaru wo enai.
Example (English): Since the deadline for this job is near, I have no choice but to work overtime.

Grammar Point: ～ずにはいられない (〜zu ni wa irarenai)
Meaning: Cannot help but; cannot resist to; always.
Formation: Verbs: Verb(ない-form) [remove ない] + ずにはいられない
Example (Japanese): この曲を聞くと、歌わずにはいられない。
Example (Romaji): Kono kyoku o kiku to, utawazu ni wa irarenai.
Example (English): When I hear this song, I cannot help but sing.

Meaning: Express the unlikelihood of something happening; 'not likely', 'doesn't seem'.
Formation: Verb-stem + そうにない, い-Adjective (drop い) + そうにない, な-Adjective + そうにない
Example (Japanese): この雨が止むそうにない。
Example (Romaji): Kono ame ga yamu sou ni nai.
Example (English): It doesn't seem like this rain will stop.

Grammar Point: ～たかと思ったら (〜ta ka to omottara)
Meaning: Express a sequence of events happening in quick succession or immediately following; 'as soon as', 'no sooner than'.
Formation: Verb-たform + かと思ったら
Example (Japanese): 電話をかけたかと思ったら、すぐに彼女が出た。
Example (Romaji): Denwa wo kaketa ka to omottara, sugu ni kanojo ga deta.
Example (English): As soon as I made the phone call, she picked up.

Meaning: Express 'since then' or 'after'; used to indicate that an action occurred once and has not been repeated or that a state has continued since a certain event or time.
Formation: Verb-past + きり
Example (Japanese): 彼は会社を辞めたきり、連絡がない。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa kaisha wo yameta kiri, renraku ga nai.
Example (English): Since he quit the company, there's been no contact.

Meaning: Expresses that something is as expected or deserves its reputation.
Formation: Verb-casual + だけあって, い-Adjective + だけあって, な-Adjective + なだけあって, Noun + だけあって
Example (Japanese): 彼は日本語が上手だけあって、日本人のように話すことができる。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa nihongo ga jouzu dake atte, nihonjin no you ni hanasu koto ga dekiru.
Example (English): As expected of being good at Japanese, he can speak like a Japanese person.

Meaning: Express a comparison; 'better than', 'at least', 'preferable'.
Formation: Verb-casual + だけましだ, い-Adjective + だけましだ, な-Adjective + だけましだ, Noun + だけましだ
Example (Japanese): 失敗するだけましだ。
Example (Romaji): Shippai suru dake mashi da.
Example (English): At least it's better than failing.

Meaning: Used to describe an action that has just been completed, often followed by a result or observation.
Formation: Verb-past + ところ, い-Adjective-past + ところ, な-Adjective + だったところ, Noun + だったところ
Example (Japanese): 掃除したところ、部屋がずっとキレイになりました。
Example (Romaji): Souji shita tokoro, heya ga zutto kirei ni narimashita.
Example (English): I just finished cleaning, and the room has become much cleaner.

Meaning: Express the moment something happens; 'as soon as', 'just when'.
Formation: Verb-past + たとたん
Example (Japanese): ドアを開けたとたん、雨が降り始めた。
Example (Romaji): Doa wo aketa totan, ame ga furihajimeta.
Example (English): As soon as I opened the door, it started to rain.

Meaning: Indicates that something is full of or covered with a certain characteristic or quality.
Formation: Noun + だらけ
Example (Japanese): 彼の部屋はゴミだらけだ。
Example (Romaji): Kare no heya wa gomi darake da.
Example (English): His room is full of trash.

Meaning: Expresses the impossibility or very low probability of something happening; 'no way', 'no chance', 'impossible'.
Formation: Verb-negative stem + っこない
Example (Japanese): こんなに雪が降っているんだから、学校に間に合っこない。
Example (Romaji): Kon'na ni yuki ga futteirun dakara, gakkou ni maniau kkonai.
Example (English): With this much snow falling, there's no way we'll make it to school on time.

Meaning: Shows two actions happening simultaneously; 'while', 'although'.
Formation: Verb-stem + つつ
Example (Japanese): 彼はテレビを見つつ、宿題をしていました。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa terebi wo mitsutsu, shukudai wo shiteimashita.
Example (English): He was doing his homework while watching TV.

Meaning: Expresses the ongoing process or gradual change.
Formation: Verb-stem + つつある
Example (Japanese): 地球温暖化は進行つつある。
Example (Romaji): Chikyuu ondanka wa shinkou tsutsu aru.
Example (English): Global warming is in progress.

Meaning: Express a continuous action or state; 'leave as is', 'non-stop', 'the whole time'.
Formation: Verb-ます stem + っぱなし
Example (Japanese): 窓を開けっぱなしにして、部屋が寒くなってしまった。
Example (Romaji): Mado wo akeppanashi ni shite, heya ga samuku natte shimatta.
Example (English): I left the window open, and the room became cold.

Meaning: Used to indicate that something has the appearance, characteristics, or behavior of something else.
Formation: Noun + っぽい, Verb-casual + っぽい, い-Adjective + っぽい, な-Adjective + っぽい
Example (Japanese): 彼女は大人っぽい服を着ている。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo wa otonappoi fuku o kite iru.
Example (English): She is wearing clothes that look mature.

Meaning: Expresses that one cannot afford to do something; 'can't keep on', 'unable to continue'.
Formation: Verb-て form + いられない
Example (Japanese): こんなに忙しいのに、無理に遊んでいられない。
Example (Romaji): Konna ni isogashii noni, muri ni asonde irarenai.
Example (English): I'm so busy that I can't afford to play around.

Meaning: Expresses that something cannot be endured, tolerated, or is uncontrollable.
Formation: Verb-てform + かなわない
Example (Japanese): この暑さにはもう我慢してかなわない。
Example (Romaji): Kono atsusa ni wa mou gaman shite kanawanai.
Example (English): I cannot endure this heat anymore.

Grammar Point: ～てからでないと (〜te kara denai to)
Meaning: Indicates that something cannot be done before a certain action is completed; 'not until', 'only after'.
Formation: Verb-casual + てからでないと
Example (Japanese): 宿題をしてからでないと、遊びに行けません。
Example (Romaji): Shukudai wo shite kara denai to, asobi ni ikemasen.
Example (English): You cannot go play until after you have done your homework.

Meaning: Emphasizes the condition; 'only when', 'precisely because'
Formation: Verb-てform + こそ, い-adjective + くてこそ, な-adjective + でこそ, Noun + でこそ
Example (Japanese): 勉強してこそ、テストに合格します。
Example (Romaji): Benkyou shite koso, tesuto ni goukaku shimasu.
Example (English): Only when you study will you pass the test.

Meaning: Can't be helped; inevitable.
Formation: Verb-te form + でしょうがない, い-Adjective + でしょうがない, な-Adjective + でしょうがない, Noun + でしょうがない
Example (Japanese): 雨が降っているから、家にいるでしょうがない。
Example (Romaji): Ame ga futteiru kara, ie ni iru deshou ga nai.
Example (English): Since it's raining, it's inevitable that we have to stay home.

Meaning: Express strong feelings or emotions; 'can't stand', 'can't resist', 'extremely'.
Formation: Verb-てform + たまらない, い-Adjective + でたまらない, な-Adjective + でたまらない, Noun + でたまらない
Example (Japanese): この暑さでたまらない。
Example (Romaji): Kono atsusa de tamaranai.
Example (English): This heat is unbearable.

Meaning: Indicates a strong feeling or emotion; 'I cannot help but', 'I cannot stand'.
Formation: い-Adjective (negative stem) + でならない, な-Adjective + でなならない
Example (Japanese): 彼の演技が上手すぎて、感動でならない。
Example (Romaji): Kare no engi ga jouzu sugite, kandou denaranai.
Example (English): His acting is so good, I cannot help but be moved.

Grammar Point: ～でばかりはいられない (〜de bakari wa irarenai)
Meaning: Cannot afford to only do something; cannot always rely on
Formation: Verb-てform + でばかりはいられない
Example (Japanese): いつも助けてもらってばかりはいられない。
Example (Romaji): Itsumo tasukete moratte bakari wa irarenai.
Example (English): I can't always rely on others to help me.

Meaning: Used to show a strong assertion or emphasis on one's opinion; 'isn't it', 'aren't you', 'right'.
Formation: Noun + ではないか, い-Adjective + ではないか, な-Adjective + ではないか, Verb-casual + ではないか
Example (Japanese): 彼は優秀な学生ではないか。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa yuushuu na gakusei de wa nai ka.
Example (English): He is an excellent student, isn't he?

Meaning: Express prohibition; 'must not', 'cannot', 'should not'.
Formation: Verb-て form + はならない
Example (Japanese): ここでタバコを吸ってはならない。
Example (Romaji): Koko de tabako o sutte wa naranai.
Example (English): You must not smoke here.

Meaning: Express the extent someone goes in order to achieve something; 'to the point of', 'even', 'so far as to'.
Formation: Verb-てform + まで
Example (Japanese): 彼は試験に合格するために、徹夜してまで勉強しました。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa shiken ni goukaku suru tame ni, tetsuya shite made benkyou shimashita.
Example (English): He studied to the point of staying up all night in order to pass the exam.

Meaning: Expresses that something is natural or expected.
Formation: Verb-て form + 当然だ
Example (Japanese): 彼は毎日勉強しているから、試験に合格して当然だ。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa mainichi benkyou shiteiru kara, shiken ni goukaku shite touzen da.
Example (English): Since he studies every day, it's natural that he passes the exam.

Grammar Point: ～というものだ (〜to iu mono da)
Meaning: Expressing a general rule or common sense.
Formation: Sentence + というものだ
Example (Japanese): 若者の熱情は尊敬するに値するというものだ。
Example (Romaji): Wakamono no netsujou wa sonkei suru ni atai suru to iu mono da.
Example (English): The passion of young people is something that deserves respect.

Grammar Point: どうにか～ないものか (dou ni ka ~ nai mono ka)
Meaning: Express a strong desire or wish for something to be possible.
Formation: Verb-negative form (〜ない) + ものか
Example (Japanese): どうにかこの仕事を終わらせないものか。
Example (Romaji): Dou ni ka kono shigoto wo owarasenai mono ka.
Example (English): Is there no way to finish this job somehow?

Meaning: Express doing as instructed or how something is; 'as', 'according to', 'following'.
Formation: Verb-casual + とおり, い-Adjective + とおり, な-Adjective + だとおり, Noun + だとおり
Example (Japanese): 先生が言ったとおりに宿題をしました。
Example (Romaji): Sensei ga itta toori ni shukudai wo shimashita.
Example (English): I did my homework as the teacher said.

Meaning: Used to list examples or express uncertainty; 'such as', 'like', 'or something like that'.
Formation: Verb-casual + とか, い-Adjective + とか, な-Adjective + だとか, Noun + だとか
Example (Japanese): 休日は映画を見るとか、買い物に行くとかして過ごします。
Example (Romaji): Kyuujitsu wa eiga wo miru to ka, kaimono ni iku to ka shite sugoshimasu.
Example (English): On holidays, I spend my time doing things like watching movies or going shopping.

Meaning: Express a specific point in time or state; 'when', 'just about', 'in the middle of'.
Formation: Verb-casual + ところ, い-Adjective + ところ, な-Adjective + なところ, Noun + のところ
Example (Japanese): 出かけるところです。
Example (Romaji): Dekakeru tokoro desu.
Example (English): I am just about to leave.

Meaning: Express 'far from', 'not just', 'not only', or 'to say nothing of'.
Formation: Verb-casual + どころか, い-Adjective + どころか, な-Adjective + どころか, Noun + どころか
Example (Japanese): 彼は歌が上手どころか、プロの歌手みたいだ。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa uta ga jouzu dokoroka, puro no utaite mitai da.
Example (English): Far from just being good at singing, he is like a professional singer.

Grammar Point: ～どころではない (〜Dokoro de wa nai)
Meaning: Not the time/place for; far from; not merely
Formation: Verb-casual, past + どころではない, い-Adjective + どころではない, な-Adjective + どころではない, Noun + どころではない
Example (Japanese): 彼の失敗を笑うどころではない。我々も同じように失敗している。
Example (Romaji): Kare no shippai wo warau dokoro de wa nai. Wareware mo onaji you ni shippai shiteiru.
Example (English): It's not the time to laugh at his mistakes. We're making the same mistakes ourselves.

Meaning: Express a hypothetical situation; 'if', 'suppose', 'assuming'.
Formation: Verb-casual + としたら, い-Adjective + としたら,な-Adjective + だとしたら, Noun + だとしたら
Example (Japanese): 明日雨が降るとしたら、傘を持って行きましょう。
Example (Romaji): Ashita ame ga furu to shitara, kasa wo motte ikimashou.
Example (English): If it rains tomorrow, let's bring an umbrella.

Meaning: Even if, despite, although
Formation: Verb-casual + としても, い-Adjective + としても, な-Adjective + だとしても, Noun + だとしても
Example (Japanese): 雨が降っても、レースは開催されます。
Example (Romaji): Ame ga futte mo, reesu wa kaisai saremasu.
Example (English): Even if it rains, the race will be held.

Meaning: Expresses 'together with' or 'along with'; used to describe two events or actions happening simultaneously or in parallel.
Formation: Verb-casual + とともに, い-Adjective + とともに, な-Adjective + とともに, Noun + とともに
Example (Japanese): 彼が来るとともに、パーティーが始まりました。
Example (Romaji): Kare ga kuru to tomoni, paatii ga hajimarimashita.
Example (English): The party started as soon as he arrived.

Meaning: Expresses that something is not necessarily true; 'not always', 'not necessarily'.
Formation: Verb-casual + とは限らない, い-Adjective + とは限らない, な-Adjective + だとは限らない, Noun + だとは限らない
Example (Japanese): いつも勉強しているとは限らない。
Example (Romaji): Itsumo benkyou shite iru to wa kagiranai.
Example (English): It's not always true that I'm studying.

Grammar Point: ～ないことはない (〜nai koto wa nai)
Meaning: Express that something is not impossible, meaning it is possible or could be done.
Formation: Verb-ないform + ことはない
Example (Japanese): 彼が来ないことはない。
Example (Romaji): Kare ga konai koto wa nai.
Example (English): It's not that he won't come (it's possible that he will come).

Grammar Point: ～ないこともない (〜nai koto mo nai)
Meaning: Used to express an action or state is 'not impossible', but emphasizes reluctance or doubt.
Formation: Verb-ないForm + こともない, い-adjective + こともない
Example (Japanese): この問題を解くことはできないこともないけど、難しいです。
Example (Romaji): Kono mondai wo toku koto wa dekinai koto mo nai kedo, muzukashii desu.
Example (English): It's not that I can't solve this problem, but it's difficult.

Grammar Point: ～ないではいられない (〜nai de wa irarenai)
Meaning: Cannot help but; cannot avoid; unable to refrain from.
Formation: Verb-ない form + ではいられない or じゃいられない
Example (Japanese): この映画はとても感動的で、泣かないではいられなかった。
Example (Romaji): Kono eiga wa totemo kandouteki de, nakanai de wa irarenakatta.
Example (English): This movie was so touching, I couldn't help but cry.

Meaning: Express doing two things simultaneously or at the same time.
Formation: Verb-stem + ながら
Example (Japanese): テレビを見ながら宿題をしています。
Example (Romaji): Terebi wo minagara shukudai wo shiteimasu.
Example (English): I am doing my homework while watching TV.

Meaning: Expresses the meaning of 'at the time of', 'in', 'on', or 'upon'.
Formation: Noun + にあたり
Example (Japanese): 入学にあたり、必要な書類を準備してください。
Example (Romaji): Nyūgaku ni atari, hitsuyōna shorui wo junbi shite kudasai.
Example (English): Please prepare the necessary documents upon entering the school.

Meaning: Indicates the place, time, or context where an action or event occurs; 'in', 'at', 'on', 'regarding'.
Formation: Noun + において
Example (Japanese): この大学において、英語のクラスが一番人気があります。
Example (Romaji): Kono daigaku ni oite, eigo no kurasu ga ichiban ninki ga arimasu.
Example (English): In this university, English classes are the most popular.

Meaning: Regardless of; irrespective of; despite.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + にかかわらず, い-Adjective + にかかわらず, な-Adjective + にかかわらず, Noun + にかかわらず
Example (Japanese): 天気にかかわらず、今日の試合は行われます。
Example (Romaji): Tenki ni kakawarazu, kyou no shiai wa okonawaremasu.
Example (English): The game today will be held, regardless of the weather.

Meaning: Indicates a specific area or aspect in which someone or something excels.
Formation: Noun + にかけては
Example (Japanese): 料理の腕前にかけては、彼女は誰にも負けません。
Example (Romaji): Ryouri no udemae ni kakete wa, kanojo wa dare ni mo makemasen.
Example (English): When it comes to cooking skills, she is second to none.

Meaning: Expresses a natural consequence or a change that occurs according to something else; 'as', 'with', 'in accordance with'.
Formation: Noun + にしたがって
Example (Japanese): 成長にしたがって、この植物の葉が大きくなります。
Example (Romaji): Seichou ni shitagatte, kono shokubutsu no ha ga ookiku narimasu.
Example (English): As it grows, the leaves of this plant become larger.

Meaning: Express a point of view; 'from the perspective of', 'if I were'.
Formation: Noun + にしたら, Pronoun + にしたら
Example (Japanese): 彼にしたら、早く帰りたいだろう。
Example (Romaji): Kare ni shitara, hayaku kaeritai darou.
Example (English): From his perspective, he probably wants to go home early.

Meaning: Expresses 'either way', 'in any case', 'be it...', used when presenting two alternatives.
Formation: Verb-てしろ + にしろ, い-Adjective + にしろ, な-Adjective + にしろ, Noun + にしろ
Example (Japanese): 行くにしろ行かないにしろ、早く決めてください。
Example (Romaji): Iku ni shiro ikanai ni shiro, hayaku kimete kudasai.
Example (English): Either way, whether you go or not, please decide quickly.

Meaning: Expresses 'whenever', 'each time', 'whether...or'.
Formation: Verb-casual + につけ, い-Adjective + につけ, な-Adjective + につけ, Noun + につけ
Example (Japanese): 外国へ行くにつけ、勉強するにつけ、言葉の壁にぶつかる。
Example (Romaji): Gaikoku e iku ni tsuke, benkyou suru ni tsuke, kotoba no kabe ni butsukaru.
Example (English): Whether I go abroad or study, I always encounter language barriers.

Meaning: Expresses the idea that as one thing changes, so does another; 'as', 'along with', 'while'.
Formation: Verb-ますstem + につれて, い-Adjective(-い) + く + につれて, な-Adjective + につれて, Noun + につれて
Example (Japanese): 年を取るにつれて、健康に気をつけなければなりません。
Example (Romaji): Toshi wo toru ni tsurete, kenkou ni ki wo tsukenakereba narimasen.
Example (English): As you get older, you have to pay more attention to your health.

Meaning: Expresses 'along with' or 'as a result of'; indicates that one event occurs along with another.
Formation: Noun (event) + にともなって, Verb-casual + にともなって
Example (Japanese): 人口が増えるにともなって、交通渋滞も悪化しています。
Example (Romaji): Jinkou ga fueru ni tomonatte, koutsuu juutai mo akka shiteimasu.
Example (English): As the population increases, traffic congestion is also getting worse.

Meaning: Express that something is 'nothing but' or 'none other than'.
Formation: Verb-plain + にほかならない, い-Adjective + にほかならない, な-Adjective + にほかならない, Noun + にほかならない
Example (Japanese): 彼の成功は努力にほかならない。
Example (Romaji): Kare no seikou wa doryoku ni hoka naranai.
Example (English): His success is nothing but hard work.

Meaning: Expresses 'despite', 'in spite of' or 'even though'.
Formation: Verb-て form + にもかかわらず, い-Adjective (drop い) + くてもかかわらず, な-Adjective + であるにもかかわらず, Noun + であるにもかかわらず
Example (Japanese): 忙しいにもかかわらず、彼は毎日運動しています。
Example (Romaji): Isogashii ni mo kakawarazu, kare wa mainichi undou shiteimasu.
Example (English): Despite being busy, he exercises every day.

Meaning: Indicates the reason, method, or means by which something happens; 'by', 'through', 'due to'.
Formation: Noun + により, Verb + により
Example (Japanese): この事故は運転手の不注意により起こりました。
Example (Romaji): Kono jiko wa untenshu no fuchuui ni yori okorimashita.
Example (English): This accident occurred due to the driver's carelessness.

Meaning: Indicates a range or extent; 'over', 'throughout', 'across'.
Formation: Noun + にわたって
Example (Japanese): 彼女は一年にわたって日本語を勉強しました。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo wa ichinen ni watatte nihongo wo benkyou shimashita.
Example (English): She studied Japanese for over a year.

Meaning: Express an action or event that occurs before another; 'before', 'prior to', 'preceding'.
Formation: Verb[ます-stem] + に先立ち
Example (Japanese): 会議に先立ち、資料を確認しましょう。
Example (Romaji): Kaigi ni sakidachi, shiryou wo kakunin shimashou.
Example (English): Before the meeting, let's check the materials.

Meaning: Contrary to, against, in spite of
Formation: Noun + に反して
Example (Japanese): 天気予報に反して、今日は雨が降っている。
Example (Romaji): Tenki yohou ni hanshite, kyou wa ame ga futte iru.
Example (English): Contrary to the weather forecast, it is raining today.

Meaning: Based on, according to, depending on
Formation: Noun + に基づいて
Example (Japanese): 研究結果に基づいて、新しい治療法が開発されました。
Example (Romaji): Kenkyuu kekka ni motozuite, atarashii chiryouhou ga kaihatsu sareました。
Example (English): A new treatment method was developed based on the research results.

Meaning: Expresses 'toward', 'against', 'in contrast to', or 'in response to'.
Formation: Noun + に対して
Example (Japanese): 日本の文化に対して尊敬の念を持っています。
Example (Romaji): Nihon no bunka ni taishite sonkei no nen wo motteimasu.
Example (English): I have a sense of respect towards Japanese culture.

Meaning: Responding to; living up to; meeting.
Formation: Noun + に応えて
Example (Japanese): お客様の要望に応えて、新しいメニューを作りました。
Example (Romaji): Okyaku-sama no youbou ni kotaete, atarashii menyuu o tsukurimashita.
Example (English): Responding to the customers' requests, we created a new menu.

Meaning: In accordance with, depending on, in response to.
Formation: Noun + に応じて
Example (Japanese): 仕事の量に応じて給料が変わります。
Example (Romaji): Shigoto no ryou ni oujite kyuuryou ga kawarimasu.
Example (English): The salary changes depending on the amount of work.

Meaning: Express certainty; 'it is obvious', 'it must be', 'no doubt'.
Formation: Verb-casual + に決まっている, い-Adjective + に決まっている, な-Adjective + だに決まっている, Noun + だに決まっている
Example (Japanese): こんなに暑い日に運動したら、汗をかくに決まっている。
Example (Romaji): Konna ni atsui hi ni undou shitara, ase wo kaku ni kimatte iru.
Example (English): It's obvious that you'll sweat if you exercise on such a hot day.

Meaning: Along with; in accordance with; following
Formation: Noun + に沿って
Example (Japanese): 川に沿って歩いていくと、橋が見えてきます。
Example (Romaji): Kawa ni sotte aruite iku to, hashi ga miete kimasu.
Example (English): If you walk along the river, you will see a bridge.

Meaning: Expresses that something is 'just' or 'nothing more than'; 'merely', 'only', 'simply'.
Formation: Verb-casual + に過ぎない, い-Adjective + に過ぎない, な-Adjective + に過ぎない, Noun + に過ぎない
Example (Japanese): 彼の失敗はミスに過ぎない。
Example (Romaji): Kare no shippai wa misu ni suginai.
Example (English): His failure is nothing more than a mistake.

Meaning: Indicates that something is related to or influenced by a certain matter or factor; 'concerning', 'in connection with', 'regarding'.
Formation: Verb-casual + に関わって, い-Adjective + に関わって, な-Adjective + に関わって, Noun + に関わって
Example (Japanese): 試験の内容に関わって、先生に質問があります。
Example (Romaji): Shiken no naiyou ni kakawatte, sensei ni shitsumon ga arimasu.
Example (English): I have a question for the teacher regarding the content of the exam.

Meaning: Expresses limitation; 'only', 'limited to', 'exclusive to'.
Formation: Noun + に限り
Example (Japanese): 今日に限り、この商品が半額です。
Example (Romaji): Kyou ni kagiri, kono shouhin ga hangaku desu.
Example (English): Today only, this product is half price.

Meaning: Used to express the moment or the occasion of an action; 'at the time of', 'upon', 'when'.
Formation: Noun + に際して
Example (Japanese): 卒業式に際して、校長先生がスピーチをします。
Example (Romaji): Sotsugyoushiki ni saishite, kouchou sensei ga supiichi wo shimasu.
Example (English): Upon the graduation ceremony, the principal gives a speech.

Meaning: Expresses obligation or necessity; 'must', 'have to', 'need to'.
Formation: Verb-ない form + ねばならない
Example (Japanese): 試験に合格するために、もっと勉強しなければならない。
Example (Romaji): Shiken ni goukaku suru tame ni, motto benkyou shinakereba naranai.
Example (English): To pass the exam, I have to study more.

Meaning: Not only... but also; as well as.
Formation: Verb-casual + のみならず + (も), い-Adjective + のみならず + (も), な-Adjective + のみならず + (も), Noun + のみならず + (も)
Example (Japanese): 彼は英語のみならず、フランス語も話せます。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa eigo no minarazu, furansugo mo hanasemasu.
Example (English): He can speak not only English but also French.

Grammar Point: ～のももっともだ (〜no mo mottomo da)
Meaning: Express that something is understandable or reasonable.
Formation: Verb-casual + のももっともだ, い-Adjective + のももっともだ,な-Adjective + なのももっともだ, Noun + なのももっともだ
Example (Japanese): 彼が緊張するのももっともだ。
Example (Romaji): Kare ga kinchou suru no mo mottomo da.
Example (English): It's understandable that he is nervous.

Meaning: Indicates 'on the basis of', 'in terms of', or 'from the standpoint of'.
Formation: Noun or Phrase + の上では
Example (Japanese): 効率の上では、この方法が最適です。
Example (Romaji): Kouritsu no ue de wa, kono houhou ga saiteki desu.
Example (English): In terms of efficiency, this method is the best.

Meaning: Under the context or condition of; under.
Formation: Verb-casual + の下で, い-Adjective + の下で, な-Adjective + の下で, Noun + の下で
Example (Japanese): 先生の下で勉強するのはとても楽しいです。
Example (Romaji): Sensei no shita de benkyou suru no wa totemo tanoshii desu.
Example (English): Studying under the teacher is very enjoyable.

Meaning: Expresses 'not only... but also'; emphasizing the extent of something.
Formation: Noun/Verb/Adjective + ばかりか + Noun/Verb/Adjective + も
Example (Japanese): 彼はかわいいばかりか賢いもです。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa kawaii bakari ka kashikoi mo desu.
Example (English): He is not only cute but also smart.

Meaning: Express a continuing state or negative tendency; 'just', 'only', 'always'.
Formation: Verb-てform + ばかりだ, い-Adjective + ばかりだ, な-Adjective + ばかりだ, Noun + ばかりだ
Example (Japanese): 彼は文句を言ってばかりだ。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa monku wo itte bakari da.
Example (English): He is always complaining.

Meaning: Express undesired situation or result caused by something; 'simply because', 'due to', 'on account of'.
Formation: Verb-casual + ばかりに, い-Adjective + ばかりに, な-Adjective + なばかりに, Noun + なばかりに
Example (Japanese): 雨が降ったばかりに、試合が中止になりました。
Example (Romaji): Ame ga futta bakari ni, shiai ga chuushi ni narimashita.
Example (English): Simply because it rained, the game was cancelled.

Grammar Point: ～ば～というものでもない (〜ba 〜to iu mono demo nai)
Meaning: Not necessarily true that if A, then B.
Formation: Verb-ば form + というものでもない
Example (Japanese): 高いものがいいものばかりではない。
Example (Romaji): Takai mono ga ii mono bakari de wa nai.
Example (English): Expensive things are not always good.

Meaning: Used to compare elements in a sentence with 'as for'.
Formation: Noun1 はともかく Noun2 は
Example (Japanese): デザインはともかく、機能はこの携帯電話が一番です。
Example (Romaji): Dezain wa tomokaku, kinou wa kono keitai denwa ga ichiban desu.
Example (English): As for design, the functionality of this mobile phone is the best.

Meaning: Expresses that although the first item is somewhat understandable or acceptable, the second item is not.
Formation: Noun1 + はまだしも + Noun2
Example (Japanese): 失敗するのはまだしも、やらないで後悔する方がつらい。
Example (Romaji): Shippai suru no wa mada shimo, yaranai de koukai suru hou ga tsurai.
Example (English): Failing is one thing, but it's even harder to not try and regret it later.

Meaning: Expressing that something is obvious or not only, but also.
Formation: Noun1 + はもとより, Noun2 + も
Example (Japanese): 英語はもとより、スペイン語も勉強しています。
Example (Romaji): Eigo wa moto yori, supeingo mo benkyou shiteimasu.
Example (English): Not only English, but I'm also studying Spanish.

Grammar Point: ～は抜きにして (〜wa nuki ni shite)
Meaning: Leaving aside, excluding
Formation: Noun + は抜きにして
Example (Japanese): 値段は抜きにして、味は美味しい。
Example (Romaji): Nedan wa nuki ni shite, aji wa oishii.
Example (English): Leaving aside the price, the taste is delicious.

Meaning: Express an action that should not be done; 'should not', 'ought not to'.
Formation: Verb-ますstem + べき + ではない
Example (Japanese): 遅れる理由がないなら、遅れるべきではありません。
Example (Romaji): Okureru riyuu ga nai nara, okureru beki dewa arimasen.
Example (English): If there is no reason to be late, you should not be late.

Meaning: Express a negative conjecture or determination; 'probably not' or 'I will not'.
Formation: Verb-ますstem + まい
Example (Japanese): 彼は今晩来るまい。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa konban kuru mai.
Example (English): He probably won't come tonight.

Meaning: Express doing something until a certain time or condition; 'until', 'to'.
Formation: Verb-てform + まで
Example (Japanese): 9時まで働いて、その後休憩しました。
Example (Romaji): Kuji made hataraite, sono ato kyūkei shimashita.
Example (English): I worked until 9 o'clock, and then took a break.

Meaning: Act according to; left as it is; unchanged.
Formation: Verb-て + まま, い-Adjective + のまま, な-Adjective + なまま, Noun + のまま
Example (Japanese): 子供が寝ているままに、静かに部屋を出ました。
Example (Romaji): Kodomo ga neteiru mama ni, shizuka ni heya wo demashita.
Example (English): I quietly left the room while the child was sleeping.

Meaning: Express indifference or disregard; 'without hesitating', 'without worrying about'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + もかまわず, Noun + もかまわず
Example (Japanese): 彼は周りの人もかまわず、大声で話しました。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa mawari no hito mo kamawazu, oogoe de hanashimashita.
Example (English): Without worrying about the people around him, he talked loudly.

Meaning: Definitely not; no way; no chance.
Formation: Verb(volitional) + ものか, い-Adjective + ものか
Example (Japanese): そんなこと、僕がやりたいものか。
Example (Romaji): Sonna koto, boku ga yaritai mono ka.
Example (English): No way I want to do such a thing.

Meaning: Express a feeling that something should be done or is expected; 'there is a need', 'there is a tendency'.
Formation: Verb-casual + ものがある, い-Adjective + ことがある
Example (Japanese): 彼はいつも遅刻するものがある。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa itsumo chikoku suru mono ga aru.
Example (English): He has a tendency to be late all the time.

Meaning: Expresses something natural or normal; 'should', 'ought to'.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + ものだ, な-Adjective + なものだ, Noun + のものだ
Example (Japanese): 若い時はたくさん遊ぶものだ。
Example (Romaji): Wakai toki wa takusan asobu mono da.
Example (English): It is natural to play a lot when you are young.

Meaning: Express the reason or cause for something; 'because', 'since', 'due to'.
Formation: Verb-plain + ものだから, い-Adjective + ものだから, な-Adjective + なものだから, Noun + なものだから
Example (Japanese): 試験が近いものだから、毎日勉強しています。
Example (Romaji): Shiken ga chikai mono dakara, mainichi benkyou shiteimasu.
Example (English): Because the exam is near, I study every day.

Meaning: Expresses 'not (something) to be done', 'should not', 'must not'.
Formation: Verb-てform + ものではない
Example (Japanese): そんなことを言うものではありません。
Example (Romaji): Sonna koto wo iu mono dewa arimasen.
Example (English): You should not say such a thing.

Meaning: Express a conditional wish; 'if only' or 'if possible'.
Formation: Verb-casual + ものなら, い-Adjective + ものなら, な-Adjective + なものなら, Noun + のなら
Example (Japanese): 時間があるものなら、この本を全部読みたい。
Example (Romaji): Jikan ga aru mono nara, kono hon wo zenbu yomitai.
Example (English): If only I had time, I would like to read this whole book.

Meaning: Indicates a contrast or contradiction between two clauses; 'although', 'but', 'even though'.
Formation: Verb-casual + ものの, い-Adjective + ものの, な-Adjective + なものの, Noun + のものの
Example (Japanese): 早起きしたものの、バスに間に合わなかった。
Example (Romaji): Hayaoki shita mono no, basu ni maniawanakatta.
Example (English): Even though I got up early, I didn't make it in time for the bus.

Meaning: Expressing that if one thing increases, the other also increases; 'the more, the more'.
Formation: Noun/Verb-て/Adjective + も + Noun/Verb-て/Adjective + ば + も
Example (Japanese): 勉強すればするも、成績が上がるでしょう。
Example (Romaji): Benkyou sureba suru mo, seiseki ga agaru deshou.
Example (English): The more you study, the better your grades will be.

Meaning: Indicates 'as good as', 'virtually', or 'practically'.
Formation: Verb-て form + も同然だ, い-Adjective + くても同然だ, な-Adjective + であっても同然だ, Noun + であっても同然だ
Example (Japanese): この運動は簡単で覚えることも同然だ。
Example (Romaji): Kono undou wa kantan de oboeru koto mo douzen da.
Example (English): This exercise is as good as easy to remember.

Meaning: Express various things or actions; 'and', 'such as', 'things like'.
Formation: Verb-casual + やら, い-Adjective + やら, な-Adjective + だやら, Noun + やら
Example (Japanese): 宿題やら掃除やらやることがたくさんある。
Example (Romaji): Shukudai yara souji yara yaru koto ga takusan aru.
Example (English): There are many things to do, such as homework and cleaning.

Meaning: Expresses that something cannot be helped or is unavoidable.
Formation: Verb-ます stem + ようがない, い-Adjective (remove い) + さがない
Example (Japanese): この仕事は終わりが見えないので、疲れるようがない。
Example (Romaji): Kono shigoto wa owari ga mienai node, tsukareru you ga nai.
Example (English): Since there is no end in sight for this job, it's inevitable to get tired.

Meaning: Express that there is no other choice/alternative; 'have no choice but', 'nothing but', 'cannot do anything but'.
Formation: Verb-Te form + よりほかない, い-Adjective-Te form(+の) + よりほかない, な-Adjective + で + よりほかない, Noun + で + よりほかない
Example (Japanese): 試験が近いので、勉強するよりほかない。
Example (Romaji): Shiken ga chikai node, benkyou suru yori hoka nai.
Example (English): Since the exam is near, there is no choice but to study.

Meaning: Expresses 'there's no way' or 'it's impossible', indicating a high degree of certainty.
Formation: Verb-casual + わけがない, い-Adjective + わけがない, な-Adjective + なわけがない, Noun + のわけがない
Example (Japanese): 彼が怪我をしたから、試合に勝てるわけがない。
Example (Romaji): Kare ga kega wo shita kara, shiai ni kateru wake ga nai.
Example (English): He got injured, so there's no way he can win the match.

Meaning: Express a logical conclusion or reason; 'it means', 'no wonder', 'the reason is'.
Formation: Verb-casual + わけだ, い-Adjective + わけだ, な-Adjective + なわけだ, Noun + のわけだ
Example (Japanese): 彼女が遅れたのは、電車が遅れたわけだ。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo ga okureta no wa, densha ga okureta wake da.
Example (English): The reason she was late is that the train was delayed.

Meaning: Not necessarily; it doesn't mean that.
Formation: Verb-plain + わけではない, い-Adjective + わけではない, な-Adjective + だわけではない, Noun + だわけではない
Example (Japanese): 彼が勉強しないわけではないが、成績があまり良くない。
Example (Romaji): Kare ga benkyou shinai wake dewa nai ga, seiseki ga amari yoku nai.
Example (English): It's not that he doesn't study, but his grades are not very good.

Grammar Point: ～わけにはいかない (〜wake ni wa ikanai)
Meaning: Expresses that one cannot afford to do something; 'cannot', 'must not', 'not allowed to'.
Formation: Verb-casual + わけにはいかない
Example (Japanese): 試験が近いから、遊ぶわけにはいかない。
Example (Romaji): Shiken ga chikai kara, asobu wake ni wa ikanai.
Example (English): Since the exam is approaching, I can't afford to play.

Meaning: indicates that something serves as a starting point or trigger for another event or action.
Formation: Noun + をきっかけに
Example (Japanese): 結婚をきっかけに、彼は真剣に仕事を頑張り始めました。
Example (Romaji): Kekkon wo kikkake ni, kare wa shinken ni shigoto wo ganbarihajimemashita.
Example (English): As a result of getting married, he began to work more seriously.

Meaning: Express 'as', 'in the capacity of', or 'taking for'.
Formation: Noun1 + を + Noun2 + として
Example (Japanese): 彼は教師を職業としています。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa kyoushi wo shokugyou toshiteimasu.
Example (English): He works as a teacher.

Meaning: Centering around, mainly, focusing on.
Formation: Noun + を中心に
Example (Japanese): このイベントは音楽を中心に楽しまれています。
Example (Romaji): Kono ibento wa ongaku wo chuushin ni tanoshimarete imasu.
Example (English): This event is mainly enjoyed for its music.

Meaning: Regardless of; irrespective of.
Formation: Noun1 + ～を問わず + Noun2
Example (Japanese): このイベントは、年齢を問わず、誰でも参加できます。
Example (Romaji): Kono ibento wa, nenrei wo towazu, daredemo sanka dekimasu.
Example (English): This event is open to everyone, regardless of age.

Meaning: To express that something is done with a certain feeling, intention, or emotion.
Formation: Feeling/emotion/intention Noun + を + 込めて + Verb
Example (Japanese): 愛を込めて料理を作りました。
Example (Romaji): Ai wo komete ryouri wo tsukurimashita.
Example (English): I cooked the meal with love.

Meaning: Expresses 'through', 'throughout', or 'during'.
Formation: Noun + を通じて
Example (Japanese): インターネットを通じて友達と連絡を取ります。
Example (Romaji): Intaanetto wo tsuujite tomodachi to renraku wo torimasu.
Example (English): I keep in touch with my friends through the internet.

Meaning: To rely on or depend on something or someone.
Formation: Noun + を頼りに
Example (Japanese): 彼女は地図を頼りに旅行をしている。
Example (Romaji): Kanojo wa chizu wo tayori ni ryokou wo shite iru.
Example (English): She is traveling relying on a map.

Meaning: Indicates that while one action is happening, another action or situation is simultaneously occurring or is in contrast.
Formation: Verbal Noun (Verb Stem) + 一方だ, Verb Stem + 一方, い-Adjective + 一方, な-Adjective + である一方
Example (Japanese): 技術が進化する一方、生活が忙しくなっている。
Example (Romaji): Gijutsu ga shinka suru ippou, seikatsu ga isogashiku natte iru.
Example (English): While technology advances, life is getting busier.

Meaning: Expresses that a situation or condition is increasingly getting more and more.
Formation: Verb-ますstem + 一方だ, い-Adjective (remove い) + 一方だ, な-Adjective + で + 一方だ
Example (Japanese): 世界の人口は増える一方だ。
Example (Romaji): Sekai no jinkou wa fueru ippou da.
Example (English): The world's population is continually increasing.

Meaning: Used to express that something is done after or on the grounds of something else; 'after', 'on the basis of'.
Formation: Verb-ますstem + 上で, Noun + の上で
Example (Japanese): 調査を行った上で、結論を出しましょう。
Example (Romaji): Chousa wo okonatta ue de, ketsuron wo dashimashou.
Example (English): Let's draw a conclusion after conducting the investigation.

Meaning: Express 'in addition to', 'besides', 'not only... but also'.
Formation: Verb-plain +  上に, い-Adjective +  上に, な-Adjective + な上に, Noun + の上に
Example (Japanese): 彼は頭がいい上に、スポーツも得意です。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa atama ga ii ue ni, supo-tsu mo tokui desu.
Example (English): In addition to being smart, he is also good at sports.

Meaning: Now that; since; once
Formation: Verb-casual + 上は, い-Adjective + 上は, な-Adjective + な上は, Noun + の上は
Example (Japanese): 試験に合格した上は、パーティーを開こう。
Example (Romaji): Shiken ni goukaku shita ue wa, paatii wo hirakou.
Example (English): Now that I have passed the exam, let's have a party.

Meaning: Expresses 'since' or 'as long as' in a conditional context.
Formation: Verb-casual + 以上, い-Adjective + 以上, な-Adjective + な以上, Noun + の以上
Example (Japanese): 彼は忙しい以上、手伝いに行っても無駄だろう。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa isogashii ijou, tetsudai ni itte mo muda darou.
Example (English): Since he is busy, it would be pointless to go help him.

Meaning: Indicates something happening 'since', 'ever since', or 'after' a particular time.
Formation: Verb-past + 以来, い-Adjective + 以来, Noun + 以来
Example (Japanese): 卒業以来、彼女に会っていない。
Example (Romaji): Sotsugyou irai, kanojo ni atte inai.
Example (English): I haven't seen her since we graduated.

Meaning: To do something completely or thoroughly.
Formation: Verb-stem + 切る
Example (Japanese): 彼は試験勉強をがんばり切るつもりだ。
Example (Romaji): Kare wa shiken benkyou o ganbarikiru tsumori da.
Example (English): He intends to study hard for the exam, doing his best.

Meaning: Express contrast between two aspects; 'on the one hand', 'on the other hand'.
Formation: Verb-casual + 反面, い-Adjective + 反面, な-Adjective + である反面, Noun + である反面
Example (Japanese): この車は速い反面、燃費が悪いです。
Example (Romaji): Kono kuruma wa hayai hanmen, nenpi ga warui desu.
Example (English): On the one hand, this car is fast, but on the other hand, it has poor fuel efficiency.

Meaning: Indicating target or intended audience.
Formation: Noun + 向け
Example (Japanese): この雑誌は若者向けです。
Example (Romaji): Kono zasshi wa wakamono-muke desu.
Example (English): This magazine is aimed at young people.

Meaning: Express a concern or fear that something undesirable might occur.
Formation: Verb-dictionary form + 恐れがある
Example (Japanese): 地震が来る恐れがあるため、避難所に行ってください。
Example (Romaji): Jishin ga kuru osore ga aru tame, hinanjo ni itte kudasai.
Example (English): Please go to the evacuation center because there is a risk of an earthquake.

Meaning: Expresses 'when' or 'in case of' specific situations or timings.
Formation: Verb-ますstem + 折には, い-Adjective + 折には, な-Adjective + な折には, Noun + の折には
Example (Japanese): 喉が渇く折には、このペットボトルの水を飲んでください。
Example (Romaji): Nodo ga kawaku ori ni wa, kono pettobotoru no mizu o nonde kudasai.
Example (English): When you are thirsty, please drink the water from this plastic bottle.

Meaning: Express the outcome after a period of time or a series of actions; 'after', 'as a result of'.
Formation: Noun + 末
Example (Japanese): 長い議論の末、ようやく意見がまとまった。
Example (Romaji): Nagai giron no sue, youyaku iken ga matomatta.
Example (English): After a long discussion, opinions finally came together.

Meaning: Expresses 'as soon as', 'depending on', or 'depending on the situation'.
Formation: Verb-ます stem + 次第, Noun + 次第
Example (Japanese): 仕事が終わり次第、帰ります。
Example (Romaji): Shigoto ga owari shidai, kaerimasu.
Example (English): I will go home as soon as work finishes.

Meaning: Depending on; based on.
Formation: Verb-ますstem + 次第で, い-Adjective + 次第で, な-Adjective + だ次第で, Noun + 次第で
Example (Japanese): 仕事が終わり次第で、家に帰ります。
Example (Romaji): Shigoto ga owari shidai de, ie ni kaerimasu.
Example (English): I will go home depending on when I finish work.

Meaning: Depends on; up to; as soon as; upon.
Formation: Verb-ますstem + 次第です
Example (Japanese): 天気次第ですが、明日ピクニックに行きたいです。
Example (Romaji): Tenki shidai desu ga, ashita pikunikku ni ikitai desu.
Example (English): It depends on the weather, but I want to go for a picnic tomorrow.

Meaning: Expresses a slight feeling or tendency towards a certain state or condition.
Formation: Verb-te form + 気味, い-Adjective (remove い) + 気味, な-Adjective + 気味
Example (Japanese): 最近寝不足気味で、ちょっと疲れています。
Example (Romaji): Saikin nebuzoku gimi de, chotto tsukarete imasu.
Example (English): Lately, I've been somewhat sleep-deprived and a bit tired.

Meaning: Expresses 'as long as', 'while', or 'to the extent of' a certain condition.
Formation: Verb-casual + 限り, い-Adjective + 限り, な-Adjective + な限り, Noun + の限り
Example (Japanese): 元気な限り、運動し続けます。
Example (Romaji): Genki na kagiri, undou shi tsuzukemasu.
Example (English): As long as I am healthy, I will continue exercising.

Meaning: Used to express the condition or situation during an event, meaning 'when', 'while', 'in the case of'.
Formation: Verb-casual + 際に, い-Adjective + 際に, な-Adjective + な際に, Noun + の際に
Example (Japanese): 出発の際に、パスポートを忘れないでください。
Example (Romaji): Shuppatsu no sai ni, pasupōto wo wasurenai de kudasai.
Example (English): When departing, please do not forget your passport.
